w:r.w:t: This section defines the OrderFood system, its users, and the external hardware and software it depends on.
OrderFood is a food delivery platform that is designed to make food ordering more transparent and affordable for customers, restaurants, and delivery agents.
The system allows the customers to browse different restaurants, place different orders, pay through virtual wallets, and track their deliveries.

Through this program, restaurants can manage their menus, they can process orders, and arrange deliveries. Delivery agents can receive their delivery requests, choose their preferred payment method, and they would be able to track their earnings.

Impact of External Systems on OrderFood

: The application must support smartphones, tablets, laptops, and desktop computers with different screen sizes. It must also be able to use location data to check the restaurant eligibility, handle payment transactions securely, and

: External APIs for maps, payments, notifications, and location tracking must be implemented. They must test compatibility across different devices, browsers, operating systems, and network conditions. Data exchanged between the systems must also be handled correctly and efficiently.

: There are cases where internet interruptions can delay the order placement or status updates. Map service failures can affect restaurant eligibility checks, payment failaures can interrupt checkout, notification delays can prevent timely updates, and server downtime can make the application temporarily unavailable. OrderFood must handle these situations without losing order details or incorrectly confirming payments.

External services may change their APIs as this happens when devices, browsers, and operating systems receive updates. The application needs requires regular testing, security updates, compatibility improvements, bug fixes, and database maintenance to ensure it continues to work correctly.

Performance and reliability: High user activity can increase the load on servers and external services. The system must be able to process orders efficiently, manage database requests, maintain accurate transaction records, recover from service interruptions, and remain reliable as the number of users grows exponentially.

Our website willl use the processing power, memory, battery, and screen of users' devices. If the website is not well optimised or is equipped with unnecessary features, it could drain the users batteries especially of the delivery drivers who would be using their mobile devices the entire day. The website must therefore be lightweight and optimised.

Our website will make use of servers (as specified in our cloud computing system before) and therefore consume lot of power. Every user interaction with the website will consume some energy and impact overall performance. Therefore, the backend of the website should be very efficient and fast to ensure minimal consumption of electricity and customer satisfaction. There should also exist backup systems and other alternatives to ensure that the website keeps on running even in certain outages.

Our website will make use of third party API services such as google maps to locate restaurants within a thirty meter radius and to help the drivers navigate. These API calls will have to be made as few times as possible to minimise operating costs and ensure that the website does not slow down. Moreover, since we would rely on third party systems, we will have to think about alternatives in case of any disruptions to the website activity.

: Similar to the Maps and location services point, our website will rely on external wallets and payment gateways to ensure legal compliance and smooth operations. However, we will have to verify that the gateway we would be using are themselves legally compliant and ensure that our website is compatible with their services. For example, our website should not have a bug where we accidentally charge the customer twice for the same meal. Such payment gateways and wallets should be deeply integrated into the website and all possible edge cases should be tested before deployment.

When a restaurant will get onboarded with us, there would be a high likelihood that the number of sales of that restaurant would typically increase over a period of few weeks. The hardware systems and software systems equipped at the restaurant should be able to cope up with the increased demand without creating a bottleneck in the entire delivery process. For example, if a restaurant is unable to cook any more food, they shouldnt be bombarded with more orders. If the infrastructure at the restaurant (which will be out of our control) fails to keep up with the demand, user dissatisfaction will extend to our website aswell.
